description: The pie chart depicts the relative share of the most frequent languages in a dataset and is divided into 10 slices, each labeled with a language name and an in-slice percentage value. The largest slice is English (dark blue) at approximately 42.8%, followed by Spanish (medium blue) at about 31.4%. Smaller slices include Russian (blue) at about 5.7%, German (lighter blue) at about 3.6%, French (light blue) at about 2.9%, Chinese (light blue) at about 2.5%, Thai (very light blue) at about 1.9%, Portuguese (Brazil) (very light blue) at about 1.7%, and Catalan (very light blue) at about 1.6%, with an “Other” category (pale blue) at about 5.8%. Percentage labels are printed inside the slices, there is no separate legend, and no slice appears exploded or otherwise emphasized; visually, the segments appear arranged roughly from the largest shares to smaller ones around the circle.
